findings.title: Current configuration is attributed to historical sessions without dated provenance
findings.what: tokenizeConfigPrefix derives a lower bound from the current live configuration, and composeSession multiplies that value across every turn of a session. The caveat says only “CURRENT” and “drift”; it carries no snapshot timestamp or artifact identifier. Consequently, the displayed historical system-prefix tokens and apportioned cost cannot be reproduced after configuration changes and are not demoted to an explicit “as of <date>” estimate.
findings.fix: Add a capturedAt timestamp or stable snapshot identifier to ConfigPrefixEstimate, propagate it into ContextComposition/provenance, and label the bucket as an estimate based on configuration “as of <capturedAt>.” Do not present it as historical per-turn attribution when no contemporaneous snapshot exists.
findings.acceptance: Given a historical session and a config snapshot captured at a fixed ISO timestamp, composition output exposes that timestamp and its user-facing provenance says “as of <date>”; changing current config without changing the supplied snapshot does not silently rewrite the historical attribution.
findings.verifyNote: Second pass re-read the calculation and caveat at lines 117-135 and the per-turn multiplication at lines 203-216. The only provenance is an undated current-config caveat; no timestamp or snapshot identity enters the estimate or composition.

findings.title: Aggregate cache hit rate cannot substantiate the claimed reclaimable write fraction
findings.what: The function claims to derive the fraction of cache-write spend that bought nothing from reads/(reads+writes), but aggregate token totals do not identify which written prefixes were later read or how often. For example, 10 written token-units with nine reads all targeting one written unit produce hitRate 9/19 and a claimed reclaimable fraction of about 5.3%, even though nine of ten written units may be unused (90%). The recommendation amount is therefore not evidence-backed or reproducible from its input.
findings.fix: Derive reclaimable spend from per-cache-entry or per-prefix write-to-read lineage. If that evidence is unavailable, remove the monetary/reclaimable claim and expose only the measured aggregate read/write ratio as a heuristic signal without a validated savings fraction.
findings.acceptance: A test fixture with identifiable cache writes and repeated reads proves reclaimable write spend from write-to-read lineage; repeated reads of one prefix cannot make unrelated unused writes appear non-reclaimable. If lineage is unavailable, no reclaimable percentage or dollar estimate is emitted.
findings.verifyNote: Second pass re-derived the formula at lines 145-157 against the measured fields at lines 117-120. Multiple distinct reuse distributions produce identical aggregate totals but different unused-write fractions, so the claimed quantity is not identifiable from hitRate.
